newsitem.title: USA: U.S. orders some embassy workers to leave Congo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. orders some embassy workers to leave Congo.

text.p: The United States on Sunday ordered non-essential U.S. embassy employees and dependents of embassy personnel to leave the Congo Brazzaville because of escalating violence in the Central African country.

The State Department also reiterated its strong recommendation, contained in a travel warning on Saturday, that Americans leave the country, citing what it called "the deteriorating security situation" and violence between elements of the Congolese military and paramilitary groups.
State Department officials were not immediately available to say how many Americans were affected by Sunday's departure order.

Sunday's revised travel warning followed the department's decision on Saturday to authorise the voluntary departure of dependents of U.S. Embassy personnel from the Congo as heavy fighting continued in the Congolese capital Brazzaville.

Saturday's warning had said a dusk-to-dawn curfew was in place, ferry service to Kinshasa was inoperable at present, and flights to and from Brazzaville are subject to cancellation or delay on short notice.
A group of 44 U.S. citizens on Saturday flew out of Brazzaville for Kinshasa, the capital of Laurent Kabila's neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.
A political militia and troops loyal to President Pascal Lissouba continued heavy fighting in Brazzaville on Sunday, sending refugees fleeing across the Congo River to Kinshasa.

There was no reliable death toll for the clashes but police sources spoke of several dozen dead and many wounded after a fourth day of bloodshed in the capital ahead of an election planned for July 27.
